title: Railway Thermite Welding Hot-Work Safety Record
description: Evidence model for aluminothermic (thermite) rail welding hot-work records: pre-ignition atmosphere verification, fire-watch, welder qualification, thermite charge control, and track-possession window closure. The thermite reaction produces ~2,500 C molten steel in-situ on the running rail, creating right-of-way fire ignition, UV/IR radiation, and molten-metal splatter hazards distinct from workshop welding. Performed during scheduled track-possession windows on Korail/SR main lines.

weld_location_kp.description: Weld site identifier: line name + kilometer post + track number (e.g., 'Jungang-Line KP 127.450 Track-2').

thermite_charge_grams.description: Net weight of the aluminothermic charge (grams). Standard 60kg-rail portion kit is ~5,000g; lighter charges indicate a non-standard kit and require engineering review.

pre_ignition_lel_percent.description: Lower Explosive Limit (%) measured at the weld crucible base BEFORE thermite ignition. Must read 0% LEL; any positive reading aborts the ignition.

fire_watch_posted.description: True if a dedicated fire-watch attendant with charged extinguisher was posted for the duration of molten-metal flow and cool-down.

welder_certification_id.description: Aluminothermic welder qualification certificate number (KorRail-approved or supplier-approved thermite welder competency ID).

cooling_time_minutes.description: Elapsed minutes between thermite tap completion and restoration of rail traffic. Minimum 15 min per KorRail aluminothermic welding procedure to ensure metallurgical set of the weld collar.

possession_window_end_iso.description: Track-possession window closing time (ISO 8601, e.g., '2026-08-07T03:10:00+09:00'). Rail traffic may only be restored AFTER this timestamp AND cooling_time_minutes have both elapsed.
